task1: well-organized glandular architecture, often forming complex cribriform or villous structures, a pushing or expansile tumor border with minimal desmoplastic reaction, and a relatively homogeneous growth pattern with uniform gland distribution.
task2: a conventional, infiltrative growth pattern with irregular, angulated glands, a dense, fibrotic desmoplastic stroma, and a relatively low density of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) within the tumor center and at the invasive front.

task1: infiltrative, irregular tumor glands with a prominent desmoplastic stromal reaction, frequent tumor budding at the invasive front, and a heterogeneous growth pattern with areas of poor differentiation, mucin pools, or signet-ring cell morphology.
task2: a prominent, dense lymphocytic infiltrate at the tumor periphery (Crohn-like reaction) and within the tumor stroma, a pushing or medullary growth pattern with well-defined borders, and frequent areas of mucinous or signet-ring cell differentiation.

task1: uniform, round to oval nuclei with fine chromatin and inconspicuous nucleoli, well-formed glandular lumina lined by tall columnar cells with apical mucin vacuoles, and a low nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, often associated with a low-grade (well to moderately differentiated) morphology.
task2: a low density of intraepithelial lymphocytes (<2 per high-power field), a lack of peritumoral lymphoid aggregates (Crohn-like reaction), and a predominance of stromal fibroblasts and collagen deposition over immune cells in the tumor microenvironment.

task1: enlarged, pleomorphic nuclei with coarse chromatin and prominent nucleoli, loss of glandular architecture with single-cell infiltration or solid sheets, abundant intracytoplasmic mucin displacing the nucleus (signet-ring cells), and a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, often associated with high-grade (poorly differentiated) morphology.
task2: a high density of intraepithelial tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs, ≥3 per high-power field) disrupting glandular structures, a prominent peritumoral lymphoid cuff, and tumor cells with a medullary or poorly differentiated morphology, often with a syncytial growth pattern and vesicular nuclei with prominent nucleoli.
